Bitcoin nearly crossed the Rubicon . Then Friday's jobs report sent the bulls backward.

Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) surged over 5% Thursday, then climbed as high as $82,000 and change Friday morning — less than $1,000 from the resistance that has capped it since February — before reversing below $80,000 .

Employers added 162,000 jobs in August , nearly triple expectations, while June and July payrolls were revised higher by a combined 55,000. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%.

The report strengthened the labor side of the case for a September rate hike by the Federal Reserve, even as cooler wage growth left inflation as the next big hurdle. Bitcoin, gold, and many of Thursday's high-beta winners turned lower as shorter-term yields and the dollar rose.

A day earlier, Waller had pushed markets in exactly the other direction.

The Fed governor opened the door to leaving interest rates unchanged at this month's meeting if inflation continues to cool.

Index futures and Treasurys climbed after his remarks Thursday morning while yields and the dollar fell. The odds of a September rate hike dropped to roughly 52% from 63% a day earlier, according to fed funds futures. The dollar posted its biggest drop since Aug. 19.

That was the day the bitcoin debasement trade took off after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent doubled planned buybacks of some longer-dated Treasurys. Bitcoin, gold, and bonds surged as the dollar fell that day as well.

Recent inflation data finally shows "some signs of disinflation," Waller said. If the improvement continues, he said he would support holding rates steady. A hot August inflation report could still put a hike back on the table.

In case the message wasn't clear enough, Waller loosened up during the Q&A.

"I'm going to paraphrase John Lennon here," he said. "Give disinflation a chance."

Strategy ( MSTR ) soared 18%, its best day in nearly seven months. Robinhood ( HOOD ) jumped 16% for its biggest gain in over a year, while Coinbase ( COIN ) climbed nearly 10%, its best day in six months.

And the enthusiasm quickly escaped crypto.

Palantir ( PLTR ) rallied nearly 8%, while the ARK Innovation ETF ( ARKK ) gained 4.5%, extending the comeback in some of Wall Street's riskiest trades .

Meanwhile, Elon Musk had a great Thursday. SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) each gained more than 5%, collectively adding nearly $200 billion in market capitalization .

articles.title: US economy adds 162,000 jobs in August
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story August jobs report beats expectations The U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs in August, soaring past expectations and raising the prospect that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates next month. AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh The unemployment…
articles.body:
The U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs in August , soaring past expectations and raising the prospect that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates next month.

The unemployment rate remained unchanged at 4.1 percent , according to the data released Friday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

Economists had expected U.S. employers to add 53,000 jobs last month and the jobless rate to hold steady at 4.1 percent, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The August jobs data marked a sharp reversal from July, which initially showed the economy losing 23,000 jobs .

However, the BLS revised jobs data from the past two months to show employers added 31,000 and 21,000 jobs in June and July, respectively.

Friday’s numbers “may corroborate that recent softness was temporary rather than indicative of a broader deterioration,” Jerry Tempelman, vice president of economic and fixed income research at Mutual of America Capital Management, said in a statement.

The better-than-expected jobs report allows the Fed to focus “squarely on controlling inflation when they meet next in September,” Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist for Fifth Third Commercial Bank, said in a statement.

This is raising the prospect that the Fed could raise rates at its meeting next month.

As of Thursday afternoon, markets saw about a 50 percent chance the central bank maintains rates at their current level and a 50 percent chance it votes for a quarter-point hike, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. By Friday morning, this shifted to about a 60 percent chance of a hike.

articles.title: Sebi clears NSE's IPO papers, to be India's biggest so far
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Friday cleared National Stock Exchange (NSE)'s offer document to go public through the initial public offer (IPO) es.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Friday cleared National Stock Exchange (NSE)'s offer document to go public through the initial public offer (IPO) estimated to be worth about Rs 30,000 crore. This will make it the largest IPO in India, ahead of Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore offer in Oct 2024.In the much-awaited NSE IPO, existing shareholders together are selling nearly 15 crore shares at a price band that would be announced before the opening of the offer. Market sources said the offer could be launched during the second half of the month.Currently, in the unofficial and unlisted space for trading of shares, mainly the IPO-bound ones, NSE shares are quoting between Rs 1,950 and Rs 2,050. If the IPO is priced at the lower end of this band, NSE, the largest bourse in India in terms of turnover and profit, would get a valuation of about Rs 4.8 lakh crore, translating to about $51 billion at the current exchange rate.In the NSE IPO, the largest seller is SBI group. While it is selling nearly 1.6 crore shares, its arm SBI Capital Markets is offloading 87.8 lakh shares. Other large sellers in the offer are MS Strategic (Mauritius), which is selling 1.6 crore shares; Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, which is selling nearly 1.2 crore shares; Aranda Investments (Mauritius), which is selling a little over 1.1 crore shares; and Bank of Baroda, which is offloading about 1.1 crore shares, offer document showed.Among the domestic institutions that are also selling part of their stakes in the IPO are Stock Holding Corp, General Insurance Corp of India, New India Assurance, National Insurance, United India Insurance and Oriental Insurance.For over a decade, NSE had been planning to go public, but faced several regulatory hurdles and court cases. Among those was the one related to some cases of preferential treatment to a group of brokers to get derivatives trading data ahead of others which were used for illegal gains. Popularly known as co-location and dark fibre cases, these were perpetrated between 2014 and 2015, and Sebi in July agreed to settle those cases against a total payment of Rs 1,491 crore. This settlement, in turn, paved the way for NSE to move ahead with its IPO plans.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Unfinished agenda larger than I thought: Axis CEO
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Under Amitabh Chaudhry, who has headed Axis Bank for seven-and-a-half years, the bank delivered an 18% ROE for nearly seven quarters. However,.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Under Amitabh Chaudhry, who has headed Axis Bank for seven-and-a-half years, the bank delivered an 18% ROE for nearly seven quarters. However, the retail cycle, higher credit costs and rate cuts put pressure on NIMs. In an interview with TOI, Chaudhry spoke about how 18% ROE remains a target, though it is aspirational and difficult to achieve.n You will be completing your third three-year term next year. What has been achieved and what is left to be done?From strengthening the brand, improving net promoter score and upgrading businesses and subsidiaries, I am satisfied with what we have achieved. But the unfinished agenda is larger than I thought a few years ago: deeper penetration, premiumisation, consistent performance, stronger deposits and capitalising on AI. Execution remains critical. Covid and the retail cycle tested us along the way. We have moved ahead of competition in payments, with strong UPI and merchant-acquisition shares and a stronger credit card franchise after Citi acquisition. We have also built the third-largest wealth franchise in four years. Retail quality has improved but remains a work in progress.Will you have to trade growth for margins?It would be the wrong approach to say, "I can either fix growth or NIMs." We can do both. Our size is not yet so large that if I have to work too much on NIMs, I have to sacrifice something else. There are times when market dynamics or external factors could impact our margins, but in the medium-to-long term, we believe we can deliver 3.8% without too much of a problem.Has Citi acquisition delivered?It has delivered. The deposit/advance portfolios, synergies and talent benefits we expected have materialised. We also received an unexpected Rs 2,000-2,300 crore tax benefit, effectively lowering the acquisition price. It strengthened our credit card and wealth franchises and added deposits when they were becoming a constraint. Given the effort required even for a small acquisition, we now believe acquisitions should be big enough to justify that effort.So you are open to growing inorganically?We are always open. We have never shied away from it. The right one needs to come along at the right price. If you look at our size, HDFC is more than double ours. We are a decent franchise with a great set of customers. If the right one comes along, we will look at it.Do you think banks have missed the bus on UPI?When people discuss UPI market share, they focus on front-end apps; banks provide the rails. Every transaction relies on banks for authorisation, funding, fraud checks, disputes, regulatory liability and customer money. Apps spent heavily to acquire customers when UPI launched, then leveraged that base to build other businesses. MDR (merchant fees) and transaction data give banks scope to underwrite, understand and reach customers better, creating a potential advantage. Axis has 35% share of the rails it provides and 20% as an issuer, making it a major player. MDR should help make UPI self-sustaining without charging consumers, while NPCI is adding more use cases to make the infrastructure more useful.But customers who earlier did not need to visit banks because of mobile and internet banking now don't need to visit the app, because large payments can be made through UPI. How do you remain relevant?UPI covers payments, but banking offers a far wider suite of services. With MDR potentially creating revenue, banks will compete harder for payments, and we are well placed with our existing share. The same shift is happening in brokerage and mutual funds.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: As protein demand rises, brands go for smaller packs
articles.summary: India Business News: Mumbai: Protein foods are now a common sight across retail shelves, but consumers may increasingly also have the choice to go for smaller-sized portio.
articles.body: Mumbai: Protein foods are now a common sight across retail shelves, but consumers may increasingly also have the choice to go for smaller-sized portions going ahead. As protein-deficient Indians become picky in terms of what they eat and add to their regular diets, companies are pushing smaller and more affordable protein packs into the market to widen consumption.From breakfast smoothies to wafers, bars and snacks-brands are making protein foods more convenient and accessible. And it's not just limited to specialised protein products; firms are also packaging foods that are naturally rich in protein in smaller sizes. ITC, for instance, recently launched chana sattu in eastern regions starting at Rs 10, which offers 10 grams of protein per pack, also tapping into regional nuances."Protein intake is not just about the quantity consumed, but also about making it easier to include protein at different consumption occasions during the day. Smaller, convenient packs can help consumers add protein across meals or while snacking rather than relying on one or two meals alone," said Hemant Malik, executive director at ITC.Consumption of protein foods today is not just limited to households that are economically well-off. A recent study by Worldpanel by Numerator showed that the lower affluent class is opting for a range of healthy snacks and beverages (including some protein snacks and drinks) for on-the-go consumption."Small-format packs can play an important role in making protein a more accessible part of everyday snacking. For consumers who are new to the category, a smaller pack lowers the entry barrier, making it easier to try, understand and eventually build a habit around protein-led products. It also fits naturally into today's on-the-go consumption occasions, whether that's a quick snack between meals, at work or while travelling," said Aditi Jain, head of brand & marketing at D2C brand SuperYou, which has introduced protein wafers and puffs across single and multi-serve packs within Rs 50. Tarun Arora, CEO at Zydus Wellness, which earlier this year expanded its range of protein snacks by adding a new millet wafer protein bar, said that today there is greater consumer scrutiny of ingredients and growing interest in protein. A 40-gram pack of the bar is priced within Rs 70.Parag Milk Foods is also widening its smaller protein snacking range with products priced at under Rs 100. "Parag Milk Foods is approaching protein consumption across multiple consumption occasions, rather than treating protein purely as a sports-nutrition category," the company said. Smaller packs are the sweet spot for consumption, said Harsch Koshti, regional marketing director, IFF Taste for Greater Asia. "The protein trend is definitely here to stay and we will see more and more specialised nutrition products designed for specific target audience, occasions and applications," Koshti added.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Discretionary spending by households rose in FY25
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: As the economy recovered from covid pandemic, household spending in 2024-25 marked a further shift towards non-essential discretionary item.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As the economy recovered from covid pandemic, household spending in 2024-25 marked a further shift towards non-essential discretionary items and services, which have earlier seen decline, signalling premiumisation and a boost for govt revenues.After seeing a decline in 2023-24, growth in household spending on alcoholic beverages, tobacco and narcotics (22.4%) outpaced growth in all other item categories to Rs 2.7 lakh crore, nearly double than what households spent on 'recreation, sport and culture' (Rs 1.4 lakh crore), the latest national accounts data released by NSO, with the revised base year 2022-23, showed.Similarly, the 'personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services' category, which has seen spending decline in 2023-24, saw a rise of 19% to Rs 5.3 lakh crore.Jewellery items, such as precious stones, wristwatches, smartwatches etc are covered under this category, along with personal care items like electric razors, hair trimmers, deodorants, sun glasses and grooming services, such as tattoo clubs, salons, spas and saunas. Travel goods like back packs and personal items like lighters, satchels and hand bags are also covered.Though the total private final consumption expenditure (PFCE) in real terms increased nearly 6% to Rs 169 lakh crore in 2024-25 - a pace similar to the previous financial year, much of this rise was cornered by services sector as share of spending on services of the total PFCE rose to 45.2% (Rs 76.3 lakh crore) as compared to 44.4% (Rs 70.5 lakh crore) previously.Among services, other categories like 'insurance and financial services' saw a 10% jump in spending to Rs 11.4 lakh crore and health saw 9% rise to Rs 8.7 lakh crore.Among essential categories, spending on food items increased 4% to Rs 45.5 lakh crore, with growth in spending on sugary products (11%), ready made food items (9%) and protein rich items like milk & dairy products, fish and seafood (nearly 7 %) outpacing cereals, eggs, fruits and vegetables. Non alcoholic beverages like soft drinks, water and juice also saw robust growth (25%) in spending in 2024-25.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: HUL plans capex boost; eyes entry into new areas
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: After two years of sluggish growth, Hindustan Unilever (HUL) is stepping up investments to defend market share amid stiff competition from a c.
articles.body: MUMBAI: After two years of sluggish growth, Hindustan Unilever (HUL) is stepping up investments to defend market share amid stiff competition from a clutch of new-age brands and changing shopping patterns. On Friday, the consumer goods giant said that it will boost capex to 3% of turnover from 2% in the last five years and "decisively" enter select high growth spaces.In its presentation to investors on Capital Markets Day, the company said that it will bet on the emerging pockets of consumption to drive expansion-a strategy the firm has dubbed internally as 'winning in new India.' "Structural shifts in new India present an attractive FMCG growth opportunity," HUL said.Last year, HUL replaced former CEO Rohit Jawa, passing on the baton to another company insider Priya Nair. Under Nair, the firm has been sharpening focus on consumer approach, crafting different strategies for different consumer classes. In a category like hair care for instance, growth in rural areas will come from increased consumption and premiumisation while in big urban cities, addition of new products to haircare routine and increased penetration will boost demand, the company said."HUL will leverage its iconic portfolio to unlock competitive volume-led growth through consumption, premiumisation, market making and entering new spaces," the maker of Knorr soups and Dove shampoos said.HUL has spent on new-age brand acquisitions bringing D2C startups such as Minimalist to its fold and is stepping up focus on distribution through quick commerce channels as consumers increasingly take to instant delivery of groceries and other household staples. In the June quarter, HUL posted an underlying sales growth of 10%, delivering its highest growth in 13 quarters. HUL's share price ended at Rs 1,974 apiece on the BSE on Friday, up 0.9%.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Federal judge allows Pentagon to fire three Stars and Stripes journalists
articles.summary: A federal judge on Friday ruled that the Pentagon can fire three Stars and Stripes journalists, the latest in a series of blows to press freedoms in the military as the agency has sought to undo the newspaper’s editorial independence.
articles.body: A federal judge on Friday ruled that the Pentagon can fire three Stars and Stripes journalists, the latest in a series of blows to press freedoms in the military as the agency has sought to undo the newspaper’s editorial independence. US District Judge Trevor McFadden denied temporary restraining order requests from Stars and Stripes publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Erik Slavin and Middle East reporter Lara Korte, allowing the Pentagon to move forward with their firings. Friday’s written ruling claims the government likely did not violate the journalists’ First Amendment rights. “Plaintiffs ultimately fail to carry their significant burden to show that they are clearly entitled to a preliminary injunction,” McFadden wrote. McFadden’s denial of the temporary restraining orders is a setback for Slavin, Lederer and Korte, who sought to be reinstated to their positions. An attorney for the trio said they were “disappointed” with the ruling. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to CNN’s request for comment. It’s unclear whether the agency has fired the trio since McFadden’s ruling. Lederer, Slavin and Korte sued the Pentagon on August 28, one week after they alleged they were illegally pushed out, accusing it of doing so over personal statements protected under the First Amendment. The lawsuit claims the Pentagon was displeased with a July 5 “CBS Sunday Morning” segment that included statements by Slavin and Korte about changes to Stars and Stripes’ independence. After the military newspaper reported on hardships aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, the Pentagon directed Lederer to push out Slavin and Korte, which he did not do, according to the lawsuit. Lederer would later announce his retirement. In his ruling, McFadden wrote that Slavin and Korte “requested and received permission from their superiors for their remarks in advance.” Later in the filing, McFadden argued that “Plaintiffs’ own pleadings and the CBS News segment suggest that they spoke as part of their official duties and not as private citizens.” “They are thus unlikely to succeed on the merits of their First Amendment claim and do not demonstrate irreparable harm,” wrote McFadden, who was appointed by President Donald Trump in 2017. In Lederer’s case, McFadden wrote that his “failure to carry out a directive from a supervisor finds no shelter under the First Amendment.” Elsewhere in the ruling, McFadden wrote that the trio’s “real complaint seems to be that they were victims of a cruel bait-and-switch.” “Perhaps discovery will strengthen Plaintiffs’ case. But at bottom, on the current record, Plaintiffs’ real complaint seems to be that they were victims of a cruel bait-and-switch,” McFadden wrote. “They are being fired for giving pre-approved interviews on their paper’s behalf in which they largely toed the company line. Whatever else such a scheme may violate, it does not clearly offend the First Amendment.” The ruling follows a Friday morning hearing, which came on the final day of a week-long reprieve from the Pentagon that temporarily stayed the trio’s terminations. McFadden’s ruling is a blow for press freedoms within the US military. Stars and Stripes, which is partially funded by the agency, has a decades-long record of editorial independence. In January, chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell posted on X that the Department of War sought to “modernize” the military newspaper’s operations and “refocus its content away from woke distractions.” That same month, the Pentagon moved to repeal the Stripes regulations that protected the outlet’s editorial independence. In addition to the lawsuit by Slavin, Lederer and Korte, the Pentagon faces two other lawsuits from individuals associated with Stars and Stripes. In early June, two advisory board members sued the agency over the “modernization” efforts, claiming they amount to illegal censorship. Later that month, the outlet’s ombudsman sued the agency, alleging First Amendment violations after being forced out in April.
